claim: The four-stage model (preparation, incubation, illumination, verification) is a descriptive label built on introspection and anecdotes, not a tested mechanism. Several famous anecdotes (Kubla Khan, Kekule) were shown false.
agent_test: Not testable as a mechanism; test only the operational parts (impasse detector, verify state) already in the schema.

claim: Averaged over 117 studies, a break after impasse gives a small positive benefit (weighted d = 0.29, CI 0.21 to 0.39), with large heterogeneity (Q = 173.99, df 113) and some null studies. Benefit is larger for divergent-thinking tasks than for linguistic and visual insight tasks.
agent_test: Not a code feature. If tested: fixed-token plain run vs the same tokens split by an off-topic filler step on insight items; expect a small effect at most.

claim: Longer preparation before the break gives a larger incubation effect (positive regression coefficient in the meta-analysis). Moderators are correlated, so a causal reading is weak.
agent_test: Vary tokens spent before the impasse detector fires; see whether a later reframe pays more after longer first attempts.

claim: Whether a low-demand filler beats a high-demand filler is contested. Sio and Ormerod: low load d about 0.52 vs high load 0.24 (k=22 vs 76). Baird 2012: undemanding task beat demanding, rest and no break (N=145). Segal 2004 found no effect of task demand or of 4 vs 12 min.
agent_test: Only meaningful for humans. The nearest agent analogue is a changed-context restart; test at equal tokens.

claim: The incubation benefit in Baird 2012 appeared only for problems seen before (repeat exposure) and not for new problems; rest alone gave no benefit. This fits assimilation of earlier-seen material, not free-floating unconscious work. Henok et al. (interactivity) show a related pattern but have no no-gap control. Gap search: Du 2025 (N=85, no control) found repeated > novel on Unusual Uses fluency (p=.006) but not on CRA (p=.72); Teng and Lien 2022 (N=90) found no mind-wandering benefit over control.
agent_test: Give the agent its failed-attempt log vs a fresh start after a break; compare on the same problem at equal tokens.

claim: A sleep benefit for insight was shown by Wagner 2004 (13/22 = 59.1% vs 5/22 = 22.7% in each wake group; chi2 = 8.54, P = .014; no-training control 25%). It carried to a preregistered nap study in a perceptual rule task (Lowe 2025, N2 85.7% vs wake 55.5%) but not to classic insight problems or magic tricks (Schoenauer 2018, N=77, p=.83 and .43).
agent_test: Sleep has no direct agent analogue; do not test. See K16 for the test-time analogue.

claim: The sleep-stage claim is contradictory. Lacaux 2021 found the benefit only at N1 (83.3% = 20/24 vs wake 30.6% = 15/49 vs N2 14.3% = 2/14). Lowe 2025 found N2 best (85.7%) and N1 not different from wake, and says it finds no evidence that N1 helps. Both used non-randomised stage groups and different tasks. Gap search found no larger or randomised stage test.
agent_test: None; background only.

claim: The REM-nap benefit (Cai 2009, RAT priming, N=77) rests on tiny cells (NREM n=6 per experiment), mixed P values (.04 vs .047) and no gain on repeated or new items. Schoenauer's naps had only 10-17 min REM and showed no effect.
agent_test: None.

claim: Cueing sleepers with sounds tied to unsolved puzzles raised solving of cued puzzles to 31.7% from 20.5% (dz = 0.47, N=57). One lab, no independent replication seen. Gap search: Beijamini 2021 found sleep helps (62% vs 24%, N=42) but cueing added nothing (56/58/57%); a 2021 follow-up reportedly supports cueing only with fixating information (unread).
agent_test: Analogue: re-surface only the cue of unsolved items from a stored log at a later turn, vs uncued items, at equal tokens.

claim: The unconscious thought advantage (distraction instead of deliberation improving decisions) did not replicate in a large test (N=399, accuracy 50.8/61.7% deliberation vs 55.4/65.1% distraction, p=.30). The meta-analytic g fell from 0.15 (CI .03 to .26) to 0.018 after trim-and-fill. Steindorf 2021 (822 participants) found the effect in two of three experiments, and its link to less deliberation vanished with thought probes.
agent_test: The schema already lists incubation by distraction as not to add (4b). Keep that rule.

claim: Intermittent conscious work during the break does not explain incubation in Baird 2012 and Gilhooly's tests (8 correlations, mean r = 0.11), but a 2025 preregistered writing study found mind wandering predicted gain only for repeated prompts and only on automated ratings. Thought reports are self-report. Segal 2004 (second-hand): break helped, break length and demand did not.
agent_test: Log whether the agent returns to the failed approach; not needed.

claim: Delayed incubation can be explained by forgetting of misleading cues (Smith), but this cannot explain benefits of immediate incubation. Similarity of break task to target task also moves results (Gilhooly 2013 cross-over; Segal's confound).
agent_test: Test a context reset that drops the failed attempt text but keeps the problem, at equal tokens, on impasse items.

claim: No study was found that directly tests an incubation delay or break in an LLM. Three agents searched independently, with rate limits and API failures, so absence is probable but not proven. Gap search update: the nearest test is Bulut 2026, which compares restart with continuing at matched tokens on MATH (continue won 9/9; 1 of 178 cells prefix-limited). Still no break or context-reset test on insight items.
agent_test: Run it ourselves if wanted: same prompt, same tokens, with and without a reset-and-return step, scored by code.

claim: In reasoning models, mid-trace 'aha' style shifts are rare and mostly not helpful: about 6.31% of 1M+ traces; accuracy 2.57% shifted vs 16.44% not shifted (N=723,200 in that analysis, mostly Qwen2.5-1.5B); the formal detector fires on 1.79%. Yang 2025 treats aha moments as real internal events using linguistic markers; definitions differ. Yang 2025 uses marker-based aha with no output-change definition and no accuracy effect size.
agent_test: Do not credit a trace for saying 'wait'. Keep G10 (reasoning text is not evidence); measure shifts by output change.

claim: Forced reconsideration (a second generation with a cue) raised math accuracy 0.322 to 0.406 (+8.41pp, N=320,000 paired samples) but only +0.45pp on crosswords and about 0 on Rush Hour. It costs a full second pass, so it is not at equal tokens. Kang 2025 found that cutting reflection after the first candidate saved 24.5% of tokens at under 2.9% accuracy loss. Gap search: no token-matched baseline in the paper; intervention tested on 7B-8B models; Llama 3.1-8B went -4.19pp on a MATH subset.
agent_test: At equal tokens: one long pass vs two short passes with a reconsideration cue only when checks or entropy flag doubt (matches G1).

claim: Offline pre-computation ('sleep-time compute') cuts test-time compute about 5x on Stateful GSM-Symbolic and AIME and lifts accuracy up to 13% and 18% when scaled; gain tracks how predictable the question is. IdleSpec 2026 reports +5 points on GAIA+FRAMES for its method, but its own sleep-time baseline gave none (Qwen3.5-4B 33.2 vs 29.4). Gap search: gain grows with question predictability (no threshold); IdleSpec baseline averages 31.0 vs 30.9 (Gemma4-E4B), 29.4 vs 33.2 (Qwen3.5-4B), 50.1 vs 50.5 (Gemini-2.5-Flash).
agent_test: Only worth testing if the agent sees repeated queries about one stored context; otherwise skip.

claim: Frontier LLMs fail at verifying their own insight answers. NazoNazo (38 models): verification failures were 5 to 39% of wrong answers. Stumpers: humans verified 100% of answers they had generated correctly, models averaged 41%, below chance.
agent_test: Check that code-based verification (G3) beats model self-verification at equal tokens on riddle items.

claim: LLM vs human on insight-type puzzles depends on the benchmark. Models beat humans on RAT (GPT-4o +0.35) and Stumpers (57.8% vs 38.15%), but trail on Japanese riddles (reasoning models 17.6% vs humans 52.9%) and Only Connect walls (about 41-45% vs about 80% F1). Contamination and language are open confounders.
agent_test: Use fresh, post-cutoff insight items for any agent test.

claim: Semantic-distance and RAT-style creativity tests do not predict LLM creative-writing quality once general capability is controlled (r drops to +0.08 to +0.28, not significant, 55 LLMs).
agent_test: Do not use RAT alone as a proxy for insight in agent tests.

claim: When humans use an LLM on convergent RAT items, guidance lowered accuracy by 10.6 points vs no LLM (95% CI -18.6 to -2.7), while answer-giving did not (p=.682). This is human-LLM interaction, not agent incubation.
agent_test: None for a single-agent scaffold.

claim: Unified cognitive models (CLARION, Helie and Sun) reproduce incubation effects in simulation, but the fits were not read in this run and press-level numbers (35.3% and 45.3% on the coin problem) are unverified.
agent_test: None.

claim: At matched total tokens, continuing a model's own reasoning prefix beat restarting from scratch in every exactly matched comparison (9 of 9) on MATH with two small models; only 1 of 178 problem-model cells was prefix-limited. Apparent breakthroughs are mostly compute compression.
agent_test: Insight items: run one long pass vs a reset-and-retry at equal tokens on frontier models before adding any reset.

claim: Early-in-trace probes that predict a run's success mostly read problem difficulty: a trace-blind difficulty proxy reaches AUROC 0.873 on 192K R1 generations and within-problem accuracy is at chance (0.496).
agent_test: Evaluate any stuck-detector within problem against a question-only baseline.

claim: LLMs over-apply inventive reasoning on riddle-like problems whose answers are literal (84.9% on genuine riddles vs 50.7% on riddle riddles; humans 50.5% vs 80.5%; 90.8% of LLM errors were inventive overreach).
agent_test: Add literal-reading checks to any reframe step.

claim: The unconscious-thought literature after Nieuwenstein 2015 is decision-task based and mixed (Steindorf 2021, N=822: effect in two of three experiments, lost when thoughts were probed). No insight-task replication was found, so incubation on insight problems rests on the meta-analysis and small studies.
agent_test: None.

claim: Sleep helps solving a video-game insight challenge (62% vs 24%, N=42) but cueing during sleep adds nothing (56/58/57%), so the Sanders 2019 cue effect has one positive lab and one null on a different task.
agent_test: Do not build a cue-resurfacing step on this evidence.
